notableFindings.nulByteCorruption: Two REAL production defects found while verifying: query/module.ts wrote the grouping-key separator as a RAW NUL byte instead of the two-character escape text, and issues/records.ts wrote CONTROL_PATTERN's hex escapes as raw bytes. The file's OWN comment had warned that a raw NUL makes Git classify the file as binary. LEAD-verified fixed: `file` now reports UTF-8 text where query/module.ts previously reported 'data'; a raw-control-byte grep over issues/** and query/** is empty. The transferable part is the DETECTION path - `file` reporting 'data', ripgrep refusing to grep a source file - because tsc and the test suites were both silent. A new variant of the known Write-tool mangling hazard, in hex/NUL-escape form rather than multibyte.

notableFindings.unrunTypecheck: CORRECTED in session 3; the original text is preserved in the field below. Original claim: packages/ui carries a `typecheck` script that NO CI job invokes, so its pre-existing type errors threaten nothing. That claim was verified against .github/workflows/ci.yml ALONE and stated about CI as a whole, and it is false at the workflow-set level: release.yml:89-90 runs `pnpm --dir packages/ui typecheck` and release.yml:93 runs the full packages/ui test suite; packages/ui/package.json additionally wires prepublishOnly to typecheck && test && build. Re-measured this session on a clean tree: `pnpm -C packages/ui exec tsc --noEmit` exits 2 with ELEVEN errors across 3 files (ConsultationBindingEditor.tsx 8, IssuesDrawer.tsx 1, test/canvas/v2-node-panel-consultation.test.tsx 2), not the 8 recorded; the file count matches, the error count does not, and that gap is left unexplained rather than reconciled away. Confirmed NOT this portfolio's doing: `git log origin/dev/0.2.0..HEAD` over those three paths returns no commits, so all three are untouched since merge base 657c546d. What actually changes: `does not threaten delivery` holds for THIS PR (ci.yml really never type-checks packages/ui) but NOT for the release workflow, which will fail on these errors at the next publish of 0.2.0 -- a dated risk, not a latent one. Disposition for this child is unchanged (out of scope, owned by the canvas/consultation surface). Transferable rule: when concluding that nothing runs a check, enumerate the workflow DIRECTORY, not the workflow you happen to be reading.
notableFindings.unrunTypecheckOriginalText: packages/ui carries a `typecheck` script (tsc --noEmit) that NO CI job invokes - CI runs only `vite build` (which does not type-check) and `vitest run`. notableFindings.ciUiSuiteGap: Found in session 3 while re-deriving the gate for task 8.2, and NOT what that task was looking for. This change's two new packages/ui component suites (store-aggregate-board.test.tsx, store-issues-view.test.tsx) NEVER RUN on the portfolio's pull request. ci.yml runs packages/ui tests in exactly one step (lines 151-156), gated on matrix.label == 'windows-pwsh-shard-1', against a HARDCODED four-file list that names local-path-picker, spaces-page, workflows-page and pipelines-page only; no other ci.yml step runs them, and the root vitest config excludes packages/ui entirely. release.yml:93 does run the full suite, so they are not unreachable everywhere -- they are invisible to the only gate that runs BEFORE the code lands. This is the third instance in this portfolio of the same defect class (a gate list frozen at one point in time silently stops measuring what the subject grows), and the first found inside CI itself rather than in a local command. Recorded, not fixed: adding files to ci.yml would put a .github/ path into this child's diff, which task 8.8 has already audited as clean of anything outside .ts/.tsx/.json/.md, and CI configuration is a portfolio-delivery concern. DECISION OWNER: whoever executes portfolio delivery. Options: (a) append the two files to the ci.yml list, (b) replace the hardcoded list with a full packages/ui run on one shard, (c) accept that these components gate only at release.
